clue.text: Newspaper's exposed detectives in harem, wrong time for a drink

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, so the paper's is THE SUN'S
something exposed is out in the open, overt

indicators.note: the detectives are placed in the middle of the jumbled harem letters
the harem is put wrong, its letters rearranged

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, home of London's detectives

explanation.surface: A tabloid uncovers police in a harem and drinks at the wrong hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion. A yardarm is the end of a ship's spar; the saying comes from sailors, who took their tot once the sun rose above it.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom, meaning the sun is high enough that a drink is acceptable, announces that drinking hour has arrived.

clue.text: Tasteless tree-hugging endeavour

indicators.note: the attempt wraps its arms round the tree, enclosing it

parts.note: to endeavour is to try; as a noun, a try is an attempt
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A sneer at eco-activists: tree-hugging as a vulgar, tasteless pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashy goods or behaviour are cheap and vulgar, lacking any refinement.

clue.text: No case for gun to change

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, so both ends are dropped

parts.note: a revolver is a type of handgun

explanation.surface: An instruction: without a holster, a gun should be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No case for' strips the first and last letters, the two Rs, from REVOLVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve is to develop or alter gradually over time, so it is a synonym of change.

clue.text: Hush-hush when in bed?

definitions.meaning: lying beneath the duvet or blankets, under the bedclothes

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet about what happens in the bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret agents work in disguise, and a sleeper lies literally beneath the covers.

clue.text: Shark cut

definitions.meaning: to shark is to swindle or fleece someone, as a loan shark does
to clip or crop, as with wool from sheep

explanation.definitionFit: A fleeced victim is shorn of money, so swindling fits; trimming fleece with blades is the plain sense.

clue.text: See 1
Honest kind of sandwich, top end, no crust, with coffee coming up

indicators.note: the crust is the outside edge, so the first and last letters of the phrase are trimmed away
in a down entry, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: decaf is decaffeinated coffee

explanation.surface: Ordering a sandwich: the top bit, crusts cut off, with a coffee to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no crust' leaves OPEN from TOP END; 'coming up' turns DECAF into FACED.
explanation.definitionFit: A frank, candid face looks honest; a sandwich served without its upper slice of bread is also so called.

clue.text: Dance music featuring Australians?

indicators.note: the answer is featured within the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A question whether dance music features Australian artists.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the Australians are birds, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: Emus are large flightless birds native to Australia, so they are Australians by origin.

clue.text: Pilot takes learner through air turn manoeuvre

indicators.note: a manoeuvre moves things about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A pilot with a learner aboard performs a turn in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pilot' looks like an aviator but is an adjective-noun sense: a test.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot scheme or pilot episode is a preliminary test before the real launch.

clue.text: Del Boy's lead character and none other turned up dignified

indicators.note: in a down entry the whole string is read upwards
the leading letter of the word is taken
other means a different form, so the four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Del Boy, the wheeler-dealer of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses, raised to the peerage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' rearranges NONE to ONNE; DEL + B + ONNE is then turned up by 'turned up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be raised to the nobility is to be given rank and dignity, so honoured and elevated.

clue.text: Let sound be heard

indicators.note: the word sound signals a word that is pronounced the same

parts.note: to let is to permit, so let means allowed

explanation.surface: A demand that a noise be made audible.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech that is audible, spoken out rather than silent, is what can be heard.

clue.text: A kind of exit on cue

definitions.text: A kind of exit on cue

indicators.note: a kind of something is a variant of it, so the letters are put into a different form

explanation.surface: An actor's departure from the stage at the prompt.
explanation.walkthrough: An execution is an exit from life, carried out at a set signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A judicial killing is a departure from the world, made on a signal from the officials.

clue.text: With ultimate skill, collecting finished vehicle

indicators.note: the outer letters gather up the word for finished within them
the ultimate letter is the last one of the word

parts.note: craft means skill or artistry
over means finished, ended

explanation.surface: Praise for a vehicle completed with the utmost skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushion-borne craft carrying passengers over water or land is a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Card players?

definitions.meaning: a playing card of the suit marked with a trefoil
a team or society of sportsmen

explanation.definitionFit: One of the four suits in a pack, and a sports team such as a football side.

clue.text: Chat room for 10s

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly
a chamber is a room

explanation.surface: A chat room set aside for people at 10.
explanation.walkthrough: 10s refers to the answer at 10-across: executions.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealed room filled with poison gas was used to carry out judicial killings.

clue.text: Only women can be cruel at name-calling

parts.note: if only women are present, there are no men

indicators.note: the letters can be made into another form, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A claim that women alone can be cruel when trading insults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name-calling' looks like insults but means calling things by names.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of naming terms in a science is its terminology, literally the calling of names.

clue.text: Europeans seeing school head surrounded by pupils

indicators.note: the pupils wrap round the single letter

parts.note: Etonians are pupils of Eton College, an English public school

indicators.note: the head is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Visitors from Europe watch a headteacher mobbed by schoolchildren.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Estonia, the Baltic republic, are inhabitants of Europe.

clue.text: Wind up opening old carriage clock on request in clockmaker's shop

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the string is read from the bottom
the opening of each word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to wind an antique carriage clock on demand at a clockmaker's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like a verb about clocks; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: This hot, dusty Mediterranean wind blows north from Africa.

clue.text: Assumption that when borders cease to exist, despot must fall

indicators.note: when the edges of each word go, only their inner letters remain

explanation.surface: A political prophecy: once frontiers vanish, the tyrant will be toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assumption' looks like a supposition; it means taking up a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousal of a cause is the adoption or taking up of it, and an assumption of a duty is the same act.

clue.text: Burrow returning yield to fill barrel for player

indicators.note: the inner letters go inside, filling the barrel

parts.note: a cask is a barrel
a sett is a badger's burrow

indicators.note: returning sends the word for yield back the other way

parts.note: to cede is to yield or give up

explanation.surface: A burrowing creature's harvest packed into a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an audio device that plays tapes, so it is a machine for playing music.

clue.text: It's a mystery why one might read Hemingway

indicators.note: the answer with the given word, read in another order, spells the author's name

explanation.surface: Puzzling over why anyone reads Ernest Hemingway.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus WHY rearranges to HEMINGWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle or riddle that cannot be explained is a synonym for a mystery.

clue.text: Current master plan

indicators.note: to plan is to arrange, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Today's grand strategy.
explanation.definitionFit: A flow of water such as a brook or a river current is a synonym.

clue.text: See 24
We hate having no backing nor covering etc

indicators.note: the outer words wrap around the inner letters

parts.note: nor means and not

indicators.note: the back of each word, its last letter, is lost

explanation.surface: We hate having no support or protection, and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no backing' drops the last E of each of WE and HATE, leaving W and HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Etc stands for et cetera, and this phrase is a casual way of saying and so on.

clue.text: One's said to live well in a sarcastic way

indicators.note: said signals a word with the same pronunciation

parts.note: living the life of Riley means living in comfort, so Riley is the name tied to living well

explanation.surface: A sarcastic remark about someone said to live well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The life of Riley' is an idiom for an easy, luxurious life.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking with dry, mocking irony is speaking sardonically, with a twist of humour.

clue.text: Part of Lord's pavilion is essentially all for one newly-wed

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letter

parts.note: a groom is a man just married

explanation.surface: A cricketing motto, all for one, at Lord's.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground; its pavilion's famous hall bears this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The grand hall in the pavilion at the home of cricket where members gather has this name.

clue.text: Start to crow, as very cautious bird

indicators.note: the start of the word is its first letter

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
wary means cautious

explanation.surface: A crow begins, nervous as any bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This large flightless Australasian bird is a relative of the emu.

clue.text: Not right to enter a property to steal a musical instrument

indicators.note: R is right, and not means it is taken out

parts.words: to enter a property to steal
parts.note: to burgle is to break into a building to steal

explanation.surface: A moral warning that breaking in to steal an instrument is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple brass horn used for military calls is a brass wind instrument.

clue.text: Accommodates forces

definitions.meaning: does a favour for, helps out

explanation.definitionFit: One who does a favour helps out; one who is compelled by duty is bound to act.

clue.text: See 1
